newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of USDA export data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher ahead of USDA export data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled slightly firmer amid expectations for moderate sales in Thursday's export and sales report, analysts said.
"Between 75,000 and 80,000 in fresh sales is more than what we need to reach 7.0 million bales," Smith Barney analyst David Brandon said, referring to USDA's export target for the 1996/97 crop.
Brandon noted talk of overnight buying from Brazil and Turkey. These sales would not appear in Thursday's report, however.
Most-active July cotton ended 0.20 cent higher at 73.65 cents per lb after trading from 73.75 to 72.45 cents. New-crop December finished 0.07 firmer at 75.94 cents.
Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots against Tuesday's official 4,372 lots.
Market sources widely expect prices to firm as the funds begin to cover short positions. NYCE noted on Tuesday that the speculators were holding a 19.3 percent net short position, as of April 25.
Brandon of Smith Barney said a move over 74.10 for most-active July could spark shortcovering. Longer term resistance was seen at 76.00 cents for July cotton.
Certificated stocks as of April 29 remained unchanged from the previous session at 220,870 480-lb bales.
